notes: Account snapshot: Veridian is a mid-market product analytics SaaS building an in-product AI assistant and smarter support triage. Started with Hosted API to validate quality/latency; now moving to Dedicated for predictable unit economics and isolation. Key asks: commit-based pricing (monthly GPU-hour equivalent or token commit), explicit burst policy (they want ability to 2x baseline for short spikes), clear overage rate that caps exposure, and a ramp schedule that lets them start at 40% commit month1 -> 70% month2 -> 100% month3. POC takeaways: Hosted POC shows good quality on open models (preference for Redwood-verified Llama 2/Redwood variants), caching reduces token spend materially. Latency target: 95th pct <250ms for short chat flows; for long summarization flows acceptable up to 1.5s average. Throughput target: baseline 80-120 reqs/sec per cluster for peak flows.
pricing_discussion_summary: Current proposal v2: three commit tiers (S/M/L) with monthly committed token/GPU hour equivalent. S: 50k tokens/day commit with 1.5x burst allowance; M: 150k tokens/day with 2x burst; L: 450k tokens/day with 2x burst and reserved surge capacity. Overage: 1.5x per-unit rate for first 20% overage, then 2.0x beyond cap unless customer upgrades. Ramp: customer requests 40% -> 70% -> 100% across three months; Redwood proposed phased billing and a credit for under-utilized commit in month1. Request from Veridian: explicit burst SLA (max duration 30 minutes per incident) and a hard overage cap per month during first 6 months. Finance is pushing for a 24-month term to secure discount; Veridian prefers 12-month with performance-based renewals.
technical_requirements_summary: Dedicated cluster in us-east-1 with VPC peering and private subnet egress. Want KMS integration for key wrapping and audit logs forwarded to their SIEM. Model routing: prefer open models with Redwood-verified variants; require automatic fallback to smaller model if latency target missed. Need prefix/KV caching enabled and guidance on batching config. Also asked for dedicated monitoring metrics exposed via Console and a weekly cost burn cadence email/report.
decision_criteria: 1) predictable cost model + clear overage guardrails, 2) ability to burst for product launches without catastrophic bill, 3) SOC2 + SSO + KMS, 4) operational observability (token-level cost breakdown), 5) 30-60 day ramp support and reseller-friendly invoicing
procurement_notes: Procurement requires three references (mid-market SaaS customers) and a DPA addendum confirming data residency. They want tiered SLAs by commit band. Request: sample SOW with commit tiers + explicit overage examples and monthly invoice simulation for expected traffic profile.
